channel.description: Simple, science-backed ideas for a healthier everyday life

item.title: Protein-Maxxing: Do You Really Need All That Extra Protein?
item.description: Protein is in everything from chips to water. Here's how much you actually need, who benefits from more, and the best foods to get it from.

item.title: Mouth Taping for Sleep: What the Science Says Before You Try It
item.description: Mouth taping is all over TikTok, promising better sleep and less snoring. Here's what the research really shows, the risks, and safer things to try.

item.title: Is Full-Fat Dairy Bad for You? What a New 12-Week Study Found
item.description: A new trial found three daily servings of full-fat dairy didn't hurt weight or cholesterol. Here's what it means, its limits, and how to choose dairy wisely.

item.title: The Best Exercise for Better Sleep? What New Research Says
item.description: A new review of 30 trials ranked yoga as the top exercise for poor sleep. Here's what the research found, its limits, and how to time workouts for rest.

item.title: Is Moderate Drinking Safe? What a Big New Alcohol Study Found
item.description: A major 2026 study found no level of drinking that's good for your overall health. Here's what it means for your holiday glass of wine.

item.title: Creamy Lemon Garlic Butter Beans: The 20-Minute BeanTok Dinner
item.description: Beans are all over TikTok. This creamy, cream-free butter bean skillet with spinach, garlic and lemon is a cheap, high-fibre dinner ready in 20 minutes.

item.title: Winter Citrus Salad with Kale and Chickpeas: A Bright Vitamin C Bowl
item.description: A colourful winter citrus salad with oranges, pomegranate, kale and chickpeas. Easy 15-minute recipe, plus what vitamin C really does (and doesn't) do.

item.title: Does Forcing a Smile Make You Happier? What a New Study Found
item.description: A new study of 1,200 people finds one smile can lift your mood, but repeated, pressured smiling can leave you less happy and more irritated.

item.title: Savory Oatmeal Bowl: The Cosy High-Fibre Breakfast Trend to Try
item.description: Savory oats swap sugar for eggs, greens and a drizzle of olive oil. Here's an easy 10-minute recipe, why it keeps you full, and tasty ways to vary it.

item.title: Japanese Walking: Does the 3-Minute Interval Trend Really Work?
item.description: Japanese walking alternates 3 minutes fast and 3 minutes slow. Here's what the research behind the viral trend shows, its limits, and how to start.

item.title: Fibermaxxing, Done Right: A Cosy High-Fibre Lentil and Bean Soup
item.description: Fibermaxxing is all over TikTok. Here's what the fibre trend gets right, where it goes too far, and a hearty lentil and bean soup to try this week.

item.title: Coffee and Dementia: What the Big 43-Year Study Really Found
item.description: A huge Harvard study linked 2–3 cups of coffee a day to lower dementia risk. Here's what it found, what it can't prove, and how to drink coffee wisely.

item.title: Winter Blues or SAD? How to Tell the Difference and Feel Better
item.description: Darker days can drag your mood down. Learn the difference between the winter blues and seasonal affective disorder, plus evidence-based ways to feel better.

item.title: Crispy Roasted Cabbage Wedges: 2026's Most Surprising Food Trend
item.description: Cabbage is having a moment. Here's an easy recipe for crispy roasted cabbage wedges with lemon-garlic yogurt, plus what the nutrition evidence says.

item.title: How Much Sleep Do Adults Really Need?
item.description: What the experts recommend, why it matters, and seven small habits that make a good night's sleep more likely.

item.title: How Much Exercise Do You Really Need? The 150-Minute Rule Explained
item.description: The World Health Organization's activity guidelines in plain English — and simple ways to hit them without a gym.

item.title: Easy Overnight Oats: A 5-Minute High-Fibre Breakfast
item.description: A no-cook breakfast you prepare the night before — plus four flavour ideas and why fibre matters.

item.title: A 5-Minute Breathing Exercise for Stressful Days
item.description: A simple, free technique you can use anywhere to feel calmer — step by step.
